answer: Retrospective Behavioral Clustering. Agents log actions; after each epoch, cluster identities by near-duplicate action sequences. A cluster whose internal similarity exceeds a threshold is flagged as one operator, and its members' rewards are pooled then discounted. Attackers can forge distinct profiles, but sustaining each one requires separate plausible histories, so per-identity cost becomes real compute and latency rather than a one-time fee. Honest agents show no echo across independent accounts, and a hollow cluster—many identities, one behavior—collapses to a single payout.
